blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Multilingual language models can give different identity judgments when the same people's names are written in different scripts. We study this effect using 601 audited identity pairs with attested Devanagari and Latin forms, holding the question and relation fixed. Qwen2.5-7B's same-person accuracy falls from 35.1% in Latin to 8.5% in Devanagari under Marathi prompts, while different-person accuracy remains above 98%. Evaluation across five models reveals distinct response biases, and reduced tokenization fragmentation does not reliably close the gap. Replicating the design on 374 audited Malayalam pairs built from the same entities reproduces the effect in a second script and language family: same-person accuracy falls to 5.3%, about half the matched Devanagari rate, while the margin still ranks matching above non-matching names at 0.925 AUROC. Latin-trained probes recover label information from Devanagari states, exceeding a string-feature baseline under similarity-matched negatives. Scalar calibration recovers 87% of the raw model-probe balanced-accuracy gap, identifying decision criterion placement as a major contributor. Activation patching localises causal sensitivity to the second entity in Qwen's middle layers; one shared sensitivity direction transfers about half the full-state margin correction. A fact-independent intervention at this site raises held-out Marathi same-person accuracy from 6.5% to 33.5%, with 98.5% different-person accuracy. Together, these results distinguish script-dependent discrimination from criterion placement and identify a causal site for improving identity judgments.
blocks.zh: 多语言语言模型可以在同一个人的名字用不同的脚本书写时给出不同的身份判断. 我们利用601个经审计的身份配对与经过验证的Devanagari和拉丁文形式来研究这种效果,并持有问题和关系。 Quen2.5-7B的同人精度从拉丁文的35.1%下降到马拉地语的Devanagari的8.5%,而不同人精度仍然高于98%. 对五个模式的评价显示出明显的反应偏差,减少象征性分散并不能可靠地弥补差距。 在374个被审计的马来亚拉姆对子上复制设计,由同一个实体建造,复制了第二个脚本和语言家族的效应:同人精度降至5.3%,约为对应的德瓦纳加里率的一半,而比值仍以0.925 AUROC在非匹配名称之上排列. 拉丁训练的探测器从德瓦纳加里州回收标签信息,在相似度匹配的底片下超过弦特征基线. Scalar校准恢复了87%的原始模型-概率平衡-准确性差距,确定决定标准位置为主要贡献者. 激活补丁对Quen中层第二个实体的因果灵敏度;一个共享灵敏度方向转移大约一半的全态比值修正. 现场的实事求是干预使被搁置的马拉地同人精度从6.5%提高到33.5%,不同人精度达到98.5%. 这些结果共同将基于脚本的歧视与标准位置区分开来,并确定了改进身份判断的因果地点。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
An identity judgment should remain consistent when the same people are presented
through corresponding names in different scripts. Yet multilingual models can
reject a matching pair in Devanagari and accept its attested Latin forms
(Figure 1 ). This matters for multilingual entity matching:
a system must connect aliases, birth names and pseudonyms even when a user’s
writing system differs from the model’s most familiar surface forms.
blocks.zh:
在介绍同一人时,对身份的判断应保持一致
通过不同脚本中的相应名称。 但多种语言模式可以
在 Devanagari 中拒绝匹配对并接受其验证的拉丁文形式
(图1). 这关系到多语言实体匹配 :
系统必须连接别名、出生名称和假名,即使用户使用
写作系统不同于模型最熟悉的表面形式。

blocks.en:
We study this problem through controlled identity verification. Both candidate
names are supplied; only their script-associated surface forms change. The
question language, people and relation remain fixed. Across 601 audited pairs,
Qwen2.5-7B’s Marathi same-person accuracy drops from 35.1% in Lat–Lat to 8.5%
in Dev–Dev, while it continues to reject almost all different-person pairs.
The contrast isolates a failure to affirm identity within a task the model can
partly solve through other surface forms. A second corpus in Malayalam, a different script and a
Dravidian rather than Indo-Aryan language, shows the effect is not specific to
Devanagari or to Indo-Aryan languages.

blocks.en:
Our analysis connects three levels of evidence. First, we establish the
behavioural gap across scripts and prompt languages, separating discrimination
from response bias. Five-model evaluation and romanization controls show why
tokenization efficiency alone is insufficient. Second, Latin-trained probes and
output-score calibration establish how much label information remains available
when the model answers incorrectly. Third, activation patching and subspace
interventions identify where that information can influence the decision.

文字和即时语言之间的行为差距,区分歧视
从反应偏差。 五模式评价和罗马化控制显示:
仅凭象征性化效率是不够的。 第二,经过拉丁训练的探测器

当模型答错时。 第三,激活补丁和子空间
说明该信息可在哪些方面影响决定。

blocks.en:
The resulting account is actionable. In Qwen, the second entity’s middle-layer
state is a strong intervention site, and a shared sensitivity direction transfers
roughly half the full-state correction. A vector learned from training entities
raises held-out Marathi same-person accuracy more than fivefold. Controls on
ranking, script condition and position explain this gain: much of it comes from
moving the decision criterion at a causally sensitive site. The script contrast
also changes discrimination, so calibration and script robustness are distinct
evaluation targets. Our contribution is a controlled benchmark and a diagnosis
that connects these targets to measurable internal computations.

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Multilingual models develop shared, English-aligned representations ( Wendler et al., 2024 ; Wu et al., 2025 ) , yet factual judgments can vary across
languages. Qi et al. (2023) examine consistency across translated
queries; Ai et al. (2025) study reference in code-mixed coreferential
statements across language families and scripts, including activation patching.
Our design fixes the question language and varies the two supplied names,
following one identity relation across behavioural and internal measurements.
blocks.zh:
多语种模式发展了共同的、与英语相一致的表述(Wendler等人,2024年;Wu等人,2025年),但事实判断可能因不同而不同。
语言。 Qi等人(2023年)审查翻译前后的一致性
查询; Ai等人(2025年)在编码混合协作中的研究参考
跨语言家族和脚本的语句,包括激活补丁。
我们的设计修补提问语言 并改变两个提供的名称,
在行为和内部测量中遵循一种身份关系。

blocks.en:
Wang et al. (2025) localise cross-lingual factual inconsistency
near the transition to language-specific final-layer representations and propose
a linear shortcut. We examine entity surface forms and find strong middle-layer
sensitivity at the second entity. Testing a related linear intervention against
output calibration and other script conditions clarifies what its accuracy gain
changes. Romanization can improve non-Latin processing ( Husain et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2025 ; Saji et al., 2025 ) ; our comparison
of automatic and attested forms separates shorter token sequences from reliable
behavioural recovery.

第二实体的敏感性。 测试相关的线性干预

变化。 罗马化可以改善非拉丁加工(Husain等人,2024年;Liu等人,2025年;Saji等人,2025年);我们的比较

行为恢复.

blocks.en:
We combine activation patching ( Meng et al., 2022 ; Dumas et al., 2025 ; Nanda and Bloom, 2022 ) with linear
probes ( Panchal et al., 2026 ) . The controlled task makes it possible to compare
label decodability, output calibration and causal transfer on corresponding inputs.

探测器(Panchal等人,2026年). 受控任务可以比较
标签可解码性、输出校准性以及相应输入的因果转移。

blocks.en:

pairs ( Vrandečić and Krötzsch, 2014 ) , each linking a canonical name to an attested
alias, birth name, pseudonym or nickname. 1 1 1 Code and corpora: https://github.com/Multilingual-entity/Entity_Identification Both names have observed Devanagari and
Latin forms. Independently varying the two spans yields Dev–Dev, Dev–Lat,
Lat–Dev and Lat–Lat. These are conventional name forms, so the manipulation
includes spelling and familiarity differences associated with script.
Each positive has a different-person hard negative, selected by occupation,
country and relation tier; 99.8% share occupation. A separate analysis rebuilds
negatives for name similarity (§ 5 ).

blocks.en:
The audit excludes identical Devanagari fields, joined aliases and parenthetical
metadata, as well as pairs whose two scripts encode different name relationships.
The retained set comprises 404 observed-alias relations and 197 relations involving
explicit name properties. Names are attested rather than generated by a
transliterator, making the Latin condition a comparison with conventional forms
of the same identity relation. This design supplies both candidates directly,
avoiding the additional requirement to generate an unfamiliar name.

blocks.en:
A second script. A Malayalam corpus covers 380 of the same Wikidata
entities, with both names given in Malayalam and in the original Latin forms.
A Malayalam speaker audited all 380 items and all 380 distractors, rejecting
six whose fields carried a generic honorific or a second alias, which leaves
374. Of the 760 Malayalam strings, 171 are exactly attested in Wikidata
Malayalam labels or aliases, 18 are spelling variants of an attested form, and
571 are machine-transliterated and then audited; none of the transliterations
was rejected. The same speaker checked the three Malayalam question templates.
Splits of 222/76/76 are inherited from a seed-reproduced split of the 601-item
corpus rather than recomputed, so no probe, vector or threshold from the
Devanagari experiments is transferred here. We evaluate Qwen2.5-7B
behaviourally on this corpus (Appendix AB ).

blocks.en:
Languages and scoring. Marathi and Hindi corpora cover the same
identities and have byte-identical Latin forms; 528/601 Devanagari pairs differ.
Each corpus is queried in its own language and English, with three paraphrases
and both yes/no letter assignments. We score the final-position logit margin m = z yes − z no m=z_{\mathrm{yes}}-z_{\mathrm{no}} without sampling. Behavioural accuracy pools
the six prompts per item and reports positive and negative pairs separately.
For entity-level probe and calibration comparisons, margins are averaged across
the six prompts before classification. AUROC measures ranking independently of
the decision threshold. Confidence intervals use 2,000 item-clustered bootstrap
resamples. Appendix Y specifies aggregation for each experiment.

Counterbalancing is also used in the knowledge and causal gates: an item counts
as known only when both answer-key assignments are correct. A fixed preference
for A or B therefore cannot qualify an item for causal analysis. Reporting both
pair polarities further distinguishes improved identity recognition from an
increase in acceptance that also admits unrelated people.

one template, with evaluation on all three templates. Frozen controls reuse the
test set without further fitting. Construction, prompts, gates and compute
details appear in Appendices A – C and AA .

The effect spans all three paraphrases and substantive relation tiers.

least-similar pairs: 31.3 points versus 21.3 in the most-similar band
(Appendix D ; Table 57 ). Thus, near-duplicate
spellings do not account for the phenomenon.

The behavioural polarity varies by model. Gemma accepts most positives and many negatives, whereas Qwen strongly favours
rejection. Using the signal-detection measure d ′ d^{\prime} to separate these biases,
the Lat–Lat advantage excludes zero for Qwen in Marathi, Gemma in all three
prompt languages and Llama in English (Appendix E ). Llama’s
Marathi and Hindi outputs exhibit fixed-letter instruction failures and are
excluded from this interpretation. Mistral-Small-24B has a 25.8-point Marathi
positive-accuracy gap, versus 6.9 for the Indic-adapted Sarvam-M-24B. Their
negative accuracies and checkpoint versions differ, making this a descriptive
family-and-size comparison (Appendix Z ).

blocks.en:
Devanagari names are tokenized roughly three times as finely as Latin names.
Fragmentation correlates weakly with the Latin-script benefit, and longer names
are harder to retrieve in isolation (Appendix F ). Nevertheless,
surface features predict script-sensitive items at only 0.56–0.60 out-of-fold
AUC, versus 0.86–0.96 after adding relation states (Table 18 ).

7.7–10.4, but replacement yields no reliable recovery. Substitution of the
attested Latin form reproduces Lat–Lat within 0.004 in all nine primary
model–language cells. The tested reductions in fragmentation are therefore
insufficient; spelling fidelity and familiarity remain relevant
(Appendix G ).

The frozen vector improves Lat–Lat too, raising Marathi positive accuracy
from 0.340 to 0.629 and English from 0.529 to 0.756. Treating both script

blocks.en:
These measurements distinguish three useful outcomes for multilingual identity
verification. Decoding tests whether states support the label; AUROC tests
whether the model’s scores separate matching from non-matching names; and
accuracy at a reported false-positive rate tests the decisions a user receives.
The probe, patch and steering experiments connect these outcomes without
assuming that improvement in one guarantees improvement in the others.
In particular, evaluating the same frozen intervention in both script conditions
reveals whether an accuracy gain also reduces their disparity. This makes the
second-entity site useful for controlled improvement and gives subsequent
interventions a concrete evaluation protocol.

核查。 解码测试状态是否支持标签; AUROC 测试

(a) 准确性,在报告的虚假阳性率下测试用户收到的决定。

假设一个方面的改进保证了其他方面的改进。
特别是,在两种文字条件中评价同样的冻结干预
显示准确性是否也缩小了它们之间的差距。 这使得
二实体场地用于控制下改进,并随后提供
干预一项具体的评价议定书。

blocks.en: 8 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 8 结论

blocks.en:
Controlled name-form substitutions expose substantial cross-script identity
matching failures. Cross-script probes, calibration and causal interventions
show that a large behavioural deficit can coexist with accessible label
information. In Qwen, the second entity’s middle-layer states provide an
effective intervention site: a shared sensitivity direction transfers about
half the full-state margin correction, and a fact-independent window
intervention raises held-out Marathi same-person accuracy from 6.5% to 33.5%
while retaining 98.5% negative accuracy. Evaluating discrimination, decision
criterion and both script conditions together makes these gains interpretable
and provides a basis for improving multilingual identity verification.

控制的名字形式替代暴露出大量横幅身份
匹配失败。 横幅探测、校准和因果干预
显示大型行为缺陷可以与可访问标签共存
资料。 在Quen,第二实体的中层国家提供了
有效干预网站:共享敏感性方向转移
半个全态差值校正, 和一个独立的事实窗口
将被扣留的马拉地语同人精度从6.5%提高到33.5%
保持98.5%的负精度。 评价歧视、决定
标准以及两个脚本条件一起使得这些收益可以解释
并为改进多语种身份核查提供了基础。

blocks.en:
Coverage. The corpus covers 601 person-name relations and two scripts,
with Marathi, Hindi and English prompts. Hindi reuses the Marathi identities
with different Devanagari renderings, testing transfer across renderings
rather than an independent entity sample. A second corpus covers 374 of the same relations in Malayalam and
Latin, with Malayalam and English prompts, evaluated behaviourally on Qwen only;
no probe, patching or intervention result extends to it. Other writing systems, entity types and factual relations require further study.

blocks.en:
Scope of the diagnosis. Detailed mechanistic results concern Qwen.
Other models provide behavioural and probe comparisons and exploratory causal
analyses, with differing response biases and effective layer ranges. The 24B
comparison matches family and parameter count but uses Mistral-Small 3.0,
whereas Sarvam-M derives from 3.1; it does not isolate Indic post-training.

blocks.en:
Information and causal interpretation. Probes establish label
decodability, and the matched-negative analysis exceeds a five-feature surface
baseline. Neither uniquely identifies retrieval of an identity association:
learned orthographic regularities and familiarity may contribute. Tight
similarity matching is available for 144/601 items. Nonce names alter response
bias as well as entity content, limiting conclusions about entity specificity.
The E2 result identifies an intervention site rather than the location of a
stored fact; local gradients describe sensitivity near the measured state.

Evaluation dependence. Target items are split into training,
validation and test sets, but globally selected distractors can cross those
boundaries (Appendix H ). The stable causal gate yields only 12–24
held-out items per language, motivating item-level intervals and descriptive
flip rates. The same held-out split was evaluated for the single-layer vector,
window vector, condition control and site control. Settings were selected on
validation and the latter controls were frozen, but these analyses share test
items and are not independent replications. The sensitivity-vector steering
sweep is validation-only and is reported separately from held-out results.

评价的依赖性。 目标项目分为培训,

romanization gives no reliable recovery and lowers performance in most cells, while the
human Latin form of
the same name makes it better (§ 4.2 ). Two models with roughly half the
Devanagari fragmentation of the third show gaps of comparable size. And out-of-fold
prediction of which items are script-sensitive reaches 0.56 to 0.60 AUC from surface
features against 0.86 to 0.96 from mid-network relation states
(Table 18 ): a per-item predictor built from token ratios is close to useless
even though the aggregate correlation is real. A covariate that explains this little per item does not account for the effect on
its own. Token ratios are an imperfect proxy and downstream representations can
carry tokenizer effects a surface count cannot see, so the defensible claim is the
narrower one: the reductions in fragmentation we tested did not restore performance.

blocks.en:
That ordering looks odd, since full is the difference between the two conditions
the task compares and additive is a sum of two partial swaps. All four are unit
length, so the difference is directional, and the cosines say what it is. Taken at the
second entity, full is close to orthogonal to the first-entity swap, cosine 0.306
under Marathi prompts and 0.200 under English, while it aligns with the second-entity swap
at 0.786 and 0.632. The two single swaps are themselves nearly orthogonal to each other,
0.292 and 0.213. So the direct Lat–Lat minus Dev–Dev difference, measured at the second
entity, is dominated by the second name’s script and carries almost none of the first
name’s: that position is where the second name sits, and the first name’s script reaches
it only through attention. Summing the two single swaps restores the first-entity
component at full weight, which is why additive is not simply a rescaling of full : the two are 43 and 57 degrees apart.

Marathi and 18 to 22 in English, rising with depth. The grid of
Appendix M stopped at 8. A sweep that never reaches half the required
distance cannot distinguish a direction that does not work from a step that is too small.
The scales that maximise positive-pair accuracy, 16 in Marathi and 24 in English, land
inside that range and just above it respectively, so the geometry anticipates the sweep.

blocks.en:
The corpus used here is a rebuild. The earlier version contained items whose two script
fields held different names rather than different spellings of one name, and
Table 50 lists examples of the failure mode. The cause was in the
construction rather than in the data: Wikidata records aliases as independent per
language lists with nothing linking an entry in one to an entry in another, and the
earlier build selected from each list separately. An item could then pair a correct
Marathi alias with a correct English alias for the same person that was not the same
name, so the Devanagari and Latin prompts asked different questions and the script
contrast was confounded with a change of name.

only that the script difference in how separable the names are is small, not that no
surface property explains the behavioural gap.

Three claims should be kept apart here. Surface information is present in the input:
the two Devanagari strings of a same-person pair are more alike than those of a
hard negative, by 0.423 in mean sequence ratio. A classifier can exploit it, reaching
0.933 and 0.946 balanced accuracy. Neither of those is a statement about the model. What
the behavioural result adds is the third claim, that the model’s own computation does not
reliably convert the available surface evidence into a correct SAME decision, since it
answers 8.5% in Dev–Dev on the same pairs a string classifier separates at 0.933. That
third claim is about the model; the first two are about the strings.

Matching cannot succeed everywhere, and the reason is structural rather than a defect of
the procedure. A distractor must be some other item’s second name, and a positive pair’s
similarity usually comes from a real relationship: an expansion that shares most of its
characters, which no unrelated name reproduces. Across all 601 items the best achievable
separation is 0.184 against the shipped map’s 0.423. On 144 of them it reaches 0.003,
which is the subset Table 55 reports; the items that resist matching are
the similar ones, mean positive similarity 0.749 against 0.409 for those that match.
Matching on all five features at once is worse still, reaching 30 items, so we report the
partial result rather than claim a matched corpus.

blocks.en:
What the comparison shows is a dissociation. Removing most of the surface signal costs the
string classifier two fifths of its margin over chance, and costs the model nothing: the
same positive-pair accuracies to within 0.1, the same threshold-free separation to within
0.01, the same 28-point script gap, and Dev–Dev negatives still rejected at 100.0 when
the distractor is as similar to the first name as the true answer is. The model is not
reading the surface the classifier reads. Two limits on how far that goes. The positive
prompts are byte-identical between the two runs, so unchanged positive-pair accuracy is
expected rather than evidence, and the weight of the comparison rests on what could move:
the classifier’s own fall from 0.933 to 0.796 and the threshold-free separation holding to
within 0.01. And matching succeeds on 144 of 601 items, so the finding is a property of
that subset. Within those limits it weakens surface similarity as an explanation of the
script gap without removing it, and it does not license the stronger claim that entity
knowledge is present and unused, which the probe still cannot establish.

The gradient lens of § 6.2 explains the single-layer behaviour it was
introduced for. It gives a reason to expect little from a
fixed direction: the correction vector is close to orthogonal to the direction the output

very little per unit of scale. That is consistent with the small recovery we observe; it

gradient describes, which is what the window result confirms: the selected step is 12
and the best is 16, against a grid that stopped at 8. The sweep of

correction vector. We do not read the ratio as a quantity the cosines predict, since a

correction vector can only work by leaving the neighbourhood the gradient describes, which
is what a step of that size does.

stage-wise resumable, and every reported figure in this paper is recomputable from the
result tables.

One note on column naming. The column named flip_rate in the
patching tables holds the fraction of items correct after the intervention, not
the fraction whose answer changed. The two coincide wherever the baseline is wrong for
every item, which holds for the single-layer, window, joint, cross-context and control
experiments, and we have verified that every flip rate quoted in this paper is a true
flip rate. They diverge for two cases. In the reverse-direction experiment the baseline
is a working Lat–Lat run and is correct on 99 percent of items, so the column there
reads as “still correct”. On negative pairs the baseline is likewise correct, and we
report that column as post-intervention accuracy rather than as a flip rate. Readers
recomputing from the result tables should use baseline_correct together with patched_correct rather than relying on the column name alone.

questions.
